passages.text: While Peter and John were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple guard and the Sadducees came up to them, greatly disturbed that they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection of the dead.
passages.sermon:
Peter and John spoke to the people.
The priests came to them.
The captain of the temple guard came to them.
The Sadducees came to them.
The priests, the captain, and the Sadducees felt greatly disturbed.
Peter and John taught the people.
Peter and John proclaimed the resurrection of the dead.
Peter and John said the resurrection comes through Jesus.
passages.original: Λαλούντων δὲ αὐτῶν πρὸς τὸν λαὸν ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς οἱ ἱερεῖς καὶ ὁ στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ οἱ Σαδδουκαῖοι διαπονούμενοι διὰ τὸ διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς τὸν λαὸν καὶ καταγγέλλειν ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ τὴν ἀνάστασιν τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν

passages.text: They seized Peter and John, and because it was evening, they put them in custody until the next day.
passages.sermon:
The priests, the captain of the temple guard, and the Sadducees seized Peter and John.
They took hold of them.
It was already evening.
They put Peter and John in custody until the next day.
passages.original: καὶ ἐπέβαλον αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ ἔθεντο εἰς τήρησιν εἰς τὴν αὔριον ἦν γὰρ ἑσπέρα ἤδη

passages.text: But many who heard the message believed, and the number of men grew to about five thousand.
passages.sermon: Many people heard the message.\r\nMany of these people believed.\r\nThe number of men who believed became about five thousand.
passages.original: πολλοὶ δὲ τῶν ἀκουσάντων τὸν λόγον ἐπίστευσαν καὶ ἐγενήθη ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ὡς χιλιάδες πέντε

passages.text: The next day the rulers, elders, and scribes assembled in Jerusalem, along with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and many others from the high priest’s family.
passages.sermon:
The next day arrived.
The rulers gathered in Jerusalem.
The elders also gathered there.
The scribes assembled with them.
Annas was present.
Annas was the high priest.
Caiaphas was there.
John was there.
Alexander was there.
Many others from the high priest’s family were present.
All these leaders assembled together.
passages.original: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν αὔριον συναχθῆναι αὐτῶν τοὺς ἄρχοντας καὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους καὶ τοὺς γραμματεῖς ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ καὶ Ἅννας ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ Καϊάφας καὶ Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἀλέξανδρος καὶ ὅσοι ἦσαν ἐκ γένους ἀρχιερατικοῦ

passages.text: They had Peter and John brought in and began to question them: “By what power or what name did you do this?”
passages.sermon:
The rulers, elders, and scribes brought Peter and John into the middle of the assembly.
They placed Peter and John in front of everyone.
The rulers, elders, and scribes questioned Peter and John.
They asked Peter and John, “By what power did you do this?”
They also asked, “By what name did you do this?”
passages.original: καὶ στήσαντες αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ μέσῳ ἐπυνθάνοντο Ἐν ποίᾳ δυνάμει ἢ ἐν ποίῳ ὀνόματι ἐποιήσατε τοῦτο ὑμεῖς

passages.text: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, “Rulers and elders of the people!
passages.sermon:
Peter stood before the rulers and elders of the people in Jerusalem.
Peter was filled with the Holy Spirit.
Peter spoke to them.
Peter said, “Rulers and elders of the people!”
passages.original: Τότε Πέτρος πλησθεὶς Πνεύματος Ἁγίου εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Ἄρχοντες τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ πρεσβύτεροι

passages.text: If we are being examined today about a kind service to a man who was lame, to determine how he was healed, then let this be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel: It is by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified but whom God raised from the dead, that this man stands before you healed.
passages.sermon:
Peter and John stood before the rulers and elders of the people of Israel.
The rulers and elders questioned them about a good deed done to a lame man.
They wanted to know how the lame man was healed.
Peter spoke to them.
He said, “Let it be known to all of you.
Let it be known to all the people of Israel.
This man stands before you healed.
He is healed by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth.
You crucified Jesus Christ of Nazareth.
God raised Jesus from the dead.
By Jesus, this man is healed and stands before you well.”
passages.original: εἰ ἡμεῖς σήμερον ἀνακρινόμεθα ἐπὶ εὐεργεσίᾳ ἀνθρώπου ἀσθενοῦς ἐν τίνι οὗτος σέσωσται γνωστὸν ἔστω πᾶσιν ὑμῖν καὶ παντὶ τῷ λαῷ Ἰσραὴλ ὅτι ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου ὃν ὑμεῖς ἐσταυρώσατε ὃν ὁ Θεὸς ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐν τούτῳ οὗτος παρέστηκεν ἐνώπιον ὑμῶν ὑγιής

passages.text: This Jesus is ‘the stone you builders rejected, which has become the cornerstone.’
passages.sermon: Jesus is the stone.\r\nYou builders rejected this stone.\r\nGod made this stone the cornerstone.
passages.original: οὗτός ἐστιν Ὁ λίθος ὁ ἐξουθενηθεὶς ὑφ’ ὑμῶν τῶν οἰκοδόμων ὁ γενόμενος εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας

passages.text: Salvation exists in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus Christ of Nazareth is the only source of salvation.
No one else can save us.
God has not given any other name under heaven to people.
We must be saved by this name alone.
passages.original: Καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἄλλῳ οὐδενὶ ἡ σωτηρία οὐδὲ γὰρ ὄνομά ἐστιν ἕτερον ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν τὸ δεδομένον ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἐν ᾧ δεῖ σωθῆναι ἡμᾶς

passages.text: When they saw the boldness of Peter and John and realized that they were unschooled, ordinary men, they marveled and took note that these men had been with Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Peter and John stood before the people.
Peter and John spoke with boldness.
The people saw their courage.
The people realized something important.
Peter and John were unschooled men.
Peter and John were ordinary men.
The people were amazed.
The people recognized another fact.
Peter and John had been with Jesus.
passages.original: Θεωροῦντες δὲ τὴν τοῦ Πέτρου παρρησίαν καὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ καταλαβόμενοι ὅτι ἄνθρωποι ἀγράμματοί εἰσιν καὶ ἰδιῶται ἐθαύμαζον ἐπεγίνωσκόν τε αὐτοὺς ὅτι σὺν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἦσαν

passages.text: And seeing the man who had been healed standing there with them, they had nothing to say in response.
passages.sermon: The leaders saw the man who had been healed.\r\nThe healed man stood there with Peter and John.\r\nThe leaders could not say anything against them.
passages.original: τόν τε ἄνθρωπον βλέποντες σὺν αὐτοῖς ἑστῶτα τὸν τεθεραπευμένον οὐδὲν εἶχον ἀντειπεῖν

passages.text: So they ordered them to leave the Sanhedrin and then conferred together.
passages.sermon:
The Sanhedrin was the Jewish ruling council.
The council members gave an order to Peter and John.
They told Peter and John to leave the council chamber.
After Peter and John left, the council members talked to each other.
passages.original: κελεύσαντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔξω τοῦ συνεδρίου ἀπελθεῖν συνέβαλλον πρὸς ἀλλήλους

passages.text: “What shall we do with these men?” they asked. “It is clear to everyone living in Jerusalem that a remarkable miracle has occurred through them, and we cannot deny it.
passages.sermon:
The leaders of the Sanhedrin spoke together.
They asked, “What shall we do with these men?”
Everyone in Jerusalem knows about the miracle.
This miracle happened through these men.
The miracle is clear to all the people living in Jerusalem.
We cannot deny this miracle.
passages.original: λέγοντες Τί ποιήσωμεν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τούτοις ὅτι μὲν γὰρ γνωστὸν σημεῖον γέγονεν δι’ αὐτῶν πᾶσιν τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν Ἰερουσαλὴμ φανερόν καὶ οὐ δυνάμεθα ἀρνεῖσθαι

passages.text: But to keep this message from spreading any further among the people, we must warn them not to speak to anyone in this name.”
passages.sermon:
The leaders of the Sanhedrin wanted to stop the message about Jesus from spreading.
They did not want more people to hear about Jesus.
They decided to warn the apostles.
They planned to tell the apostles not to speak to anyone about Jesus.
They wanted the apostles to stop using the name of Jesus when they spoke to people.
passages.original: ἀλλ’ ἵνα μὴ ἐπὶ πλεῖον διανεμηθῇ εἰς τὸν λαόν ἀπειλησώμεθα αὐτοῖς μηκέτι λαλεῖν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ μηδενὶ ἀνθρώπων

passages.text: Then they called them in again and commanded them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus.
passages.sermon:
The Jewish leaders called Peter and John in again.
They gave them a command.
They told them not to speak at all in the name of Jesus.
They also told them not to teach anyone in the name of Jesus.
passages.original: Καὶ καλέσαντες αὐτοὺς παρήγγειλαν τὸ καθόλου μὴ φθέγγεσθαι μηδὲ διδάσκειν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: But Peter and John replied, “Judge for yourselves whether it is right in God’s sight to listen to you rather than God.
passages.sermon:
Peter and John stood before the leaders.
Peter and John answered the leaders.
Peter and John spoke directly to them.
Peter and John said, “You must decide this.
Ask yourselves if it is right before God.
Should we listen to you more than to God?
You must judge this for yourselves.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος καὶ Ἰωάννης ἀποκριθέντες εἶπον πρὸς αὐτούς Εἰ δίκαιόν ἐστιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ ὑμῶν ἀκούειν μᾶλλον ἢ τοῦ Θεοῦ κρίνατε

passages.text: For we cannot stop speaking about what we have seen and heard.”
passages.sermon:
Peter and John spoke to the leaders.
Peter and John had seen and heard important things about Jesus.
Peter and John could not stop talking about these things.
Peter and John had to speak about what they had seen and heard.
passages.original: οὐ δυνάμεθα γὰρ ἡμεῖς ἃ εἴδαμεν καὶ ἠκούσαμεν μὴ λαλεῖν

passages.text: After further threats they let them go. They could not find a way to punish them, because all the people were glorifying God for what had happened.
passages.sermon:
The Jewish leaders threatened Peter and John again.
They released Peter and John.
The leaders could not find a way to punish them.
All the people were glorifying God for what had happened.
The people praised God because of the miracle.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ προσαπειλησάμενοι ἀπέλυσαν αὐτούς μηδὲν εὑρίσκοντες τὸ πῶς κολάσωνται αὐτούς διὰ τὸν λαόν ὅτι πάντες ἐδόξαζον τὸν Θεὸν ἐπὶ τῷ γεγονότι

passages.text: For the man who was miraculously healed was over forty years old.
passages.sermon: A man was healed by a miracle.\r\nThis man was over forty years old.
passages.original: ἐτῶν γὰρ ἦν πλειόνων τεσσεράκοντα ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐφ’ ὃν γεγόνει τὸ σημεῖον τοῦτο τῆς ἰάσεως

passages.text: On their release, Peter and John returned to their own people and reported everything that the chief priests and elders had said to them.
passages.sermon:
Peter and John had been released.
They went back to their own group of believers.
They told their group everything the chief priests had said to them.
They also reported all that the elders had spoken to them.
passages.original: Ἀπολυθέντες δὲ ἦλθον πρὸς τοὺς ἰδίους καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν ὅσα πρὸς αὐτοὺς οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι εἶπαν

passages.text: When the believers heard this, they lifted up their voices to God with one accord. “Sovereign Lord,” they said, “You made the heaven and the earth and the sea and everything in them.
passages.sermon:
The believers heard the report from Peter and John.
They responded together.
They lifted their voices to God.
They spoke with one accord.
They said, “Sovereign Lord, you made the heaven.
You made the earth.
You made the sea.
You made everything in them.”
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἦραν φωνὴν πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν καὶ εἶπαν Δέσποτα σὺ ὁ ποιήσας τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς

passages.text: You spoke by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of Your servant, our father David: ‘Why do the nations rage and the peoples plot in vain?
passages.sermon:
God spoke by the Holy Spirit.
God used the mouth of David.
David was God’s servant.
David was our father.
God said, “Why do the nations rage?”
God said, “Why do the peoples plot in vain?”
passages.original: ὁ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν διὰ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου στόματος Δαυὶδ παιδός σου εἰπών Ἵνα‿ Τί ἐφρύαξαν ἔθνη καὶ λαοὶ ἐμελέτησαν κενά

passages.text: The kings of the earth take their stand and the rulers gather together against the Lord and against His Anointed One.’
passages.sermon:
The kings of the earth take their stand.
The rulers gather together.
They stand against the Lord.
They stand against His Anointed One.
passages.original: παρέστησαν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ κατὰ τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ κατὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: In fact, this is the very city where Herod and Pontius Pilate conspired with the Gentiles and the people of Israel against Your holy servant Jesus, whom You anointed.
passages.sermon:
Herod and Pontius Pilate acted in this city.
They joined with the Gentiles.
They joined with the people of Israel.
They opposed Jesus.
Jesus is Your holy servant.
You anointed Jesus.
passages.original: Συνήχθησαν γὰρ ἐπ’ ἀληθείας ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ ἐπὶ τὸν ἅγιον Παῖδά σου Ἰησοῦν ὃν ἔχρισας Ἡρῴδης τε καὶ Πόντιος Πιλᾶτος σὺν ἔθνεσιν καὶ λαοῖς Ἰσραήλ

passages.text: They carried out what Your hand and will had decided beforehand would happen.
passages.sermon:
God decided what would happen before it happened.
God’s hand and God’s will set these things in place.
The people did what God had already planned.
They carried out what God had decided.
passages.original: ποιῆσαι ὅσα ἡ χείρ σου καὶ ἡ βουλὴ σου προώρισεν γενέσθαι

passages.text: And now, Lord, consider their threats, and enable Your servants to speak Your word with complete boldness, as You stretch out Your hand to heal and perform signs and wonders through the name of Your holy servant Jesus.”
passages.sermon:
Lord, You are the one we pray to now.
You see the threats against us.
We ask You to look at these threats.
We are Your servants.
Give us courage to speak Your word.
Let us speak with complete boldness.
You have power to heal.
You stretch out Your hand to heal people.
You perform signs and wonders.
You do these things through the name of Jesus.
Jesus is Your holy servant.
You have anointed Jesus.
passages.original: καὶ τὰ νῦν Κύριε ἔπιδε ἐπὶ τὰς ἀπειλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ δὸς τοῖς δούλοις σου μετὰ παρρησίας πάσης λαλεῖν τὸν λόγον σου ἐν τῷ τὴν χεῖρά σου ἐκτείνειν σε εἰς ἴασιν καὶ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γίνεσθαι διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ ἁγίου Παιδός σου Ἰησοῦ

passages.text: After they had prayed, their meeting place was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God boldly.
passages.sermon:
The believers gathered together in one place.
They prayed to God.
After they prayed, the place where they met shook.
God filled every person there with the Holy Spirit.
They all spoke the word of God.
They spoke with boldness.
passages.original: Καὶ δεηθέντων αὐτῶν ἐσαλεύθη ὁ τόπος ἐν ᾧ ἦσαν συνηγμένοι καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν ἅπαντες τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος καὶ ἐλάλουν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ μετὰ παρρησίας

passages.text: The multitude of believers was one in heart and soul. No one claimed that any of his possessions was his own, but they shared everything they owned.
passages.sermon:
The believers formed a large group.
They all trusted in Jesus.
They were united in heart.
They were united in soul.
No one said, “This is mine.”
No one claimed any possession as his own.
They shared everything they had.
All things belonged to them together.
passages.original: Τοῦ δὲ πλήθους τῶν πιστευσάντων ἦν καρδία καὶ ψυχὴ μία καὶ οὐδὲ εἷς τι τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ ἔλεγεν ἴδιον εἶναι ἀλλ’ ἦν αὐτοῖς πάντα κοινά

passages.text: With great power the apostles continued to give their testimony about the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And abundant grace was upon them all.
passages.sermon:
The apostles followed Jesus Christ.
The apostles spoke about the resurrection of the Lord Jesus.
The apostles gave their testimony with great power.
God gave abundant grace to all the believers.
passages.original: καὶ δυνάμει μεγάλῃ ἀπεδίδουν τὸ μαρτύριον οἱ ἀπόστολοι τοῦ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ τῆς ἀναστάσεως χάρις τε μεγάλη ἦν ἐπὶ πάντας αὐτούς

passages.text: There were no needy ones among them, because those who owned lands or houses would sell their property, bring the proceeds from the sales, and lay them at the apostles’ feet for distribution to anyone as he had need.
passages.sermon:
The believers formed a community.
No one among them was needy.
Some believers owned land or houses.
These owners sold their property.
They brought the money from the sales.
They placed the money at the apostles’ feet.
The apostles distributed the money.
Each person received what he needed.
passages.original: Οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐνδεής τις ἦν ἐν αὐτοῖς ὅσοι γὰρ κτήτορες χωρίων ἢ οἰκιῶν ὑπῆρχον πωλοῦντες ἔφερον τὰς τιμὰς τῶν πιπρασκομένων καὶ ἐτίθουν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων διεδίδετο δὲ ἑκάστῳ καθότι ἄν τις χρείαν εἶχεν

passages.text: Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, whom the apostles called Barnabas (meaning Son of Encouragement), sold a field he owned, brought the money, and laid it at the apostles’ feet.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a Levite from Cyprus.
The apostles called him Barnabas.
Barnabas means Son of Encouragement.
Joseph owned a field.
He sold the field.
He brought the money from the sale.
He laid the money at the apostles’ feet.
passages.original: Ἰωσὴφ δὲ ὁ ἐπικληθεὶς Βαρνάβας ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Υἱὸς παρακλήσεως Λευίτης Κύπριος τῷ γένει ὑπάρχοντος αὐτῷ ἀγροῦ πωλήσας ἤνεγκεν τὸ χρῆμα καὶ ἔθηκεν πρὸς τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων
